cycles.title: The Furthest Remembered
cycles.description: The furthest represented past already has old guardians, towns, schools and governments. A village gift and a magical champion occupy different reaches; urban life is ancient here too.
cycles.sequenceNote: First represented turn, not the world's origin. Local centuries remain inside their stories; the order between independent societies is proposed.

cycles.title: The Second Horizon
cycles.description: Another kingdom and a modern sky crowded with magical girls precede communities living beside much older powers. That public modernity has a distant place before Northbridge and the Bay.
cycles.sequenceNote: Not About That begins the longer proposed magical-girl chronology here. Its distance from Northbridge is editorial, not a dated institutional lineage.

cycles.title: The Long Afterlight
cycles.description: Royal inheritances, engineered wonders and laboratory lives precede the quieter modernity reached by Nell and Bash. Their ordinary-looking world occupies one reach of a much older, uneven magical history.
cycles.sequenceNote: Nell and Bash's material endpoint precedes the Glass Sea. Ravel keeps its unresolved coordinate; its temporal crossing is not flattened into this cycle.

cycles.title: The Returning Years
cycles.description: New courts and teaching traditions share a proposed turn with Northbridge's magical girls. Kethra's episodes keep one human-scale sequence; Northbridge's three-afternoon continuation keeps another.
cycles.sequenceNote: Distinct local sequences within a proposed turn. Northbridge is placed after the earlier crowded sky and before the Bay without inventing a shared organization or surviving cast.

cycles.title: The Bay and Its Centuries
cycles.description: Older bargains and training histories give way to the Bay's local arc. The battle, false survivor claim and centuries-later museum occupy separate points, followed by other proposed histories before the Glass Sea.
cycles.sequenceNote: Bay, Dress and Count remain in one cycle: their interval is local centuries, not successive galactic orbits. Count's pre-extinction side is proposed; its centuries-after-Bay relation is explicit.

cycles.title: The Last Old Turn
cycles.description: The Glass Sea follows the earlier modernities. Kingdoms, private curses, a long imprisonment and Faris's thirty-one-year accumulation occupy separate reaches of the final represented old turn.
cycles.sequenceNote: The Daughter's four-century history and Ninepin's pre-extinction campaign precede All Accounts Due. The boundary ends old magic; none of these systems is carried through the zero.

cycles.title: The First Unlit Turn
cycles.description: A reactor city falls in a world that remembers magic as long dead. Independent caravans, houses, bodily technologies and an orbital watch occupy an early proposed part of the long material history.
cycles.sequenceNote: Extinction need not erase machinery, biology or civilization. These material societies retain separate histories; their different falls have no established common cause.

cycles.title: Another World of Days
cycles.description: Courts and engineering reappear; familiar streets precede layered cities and bodily reconstruction. Elsewhere a sunshade is inhabited, ruins are salvaged and a caregiver counts eighteen years.
cycles.sequenceNote: The turn follows the preceding material histories provisionally. The orbital machinery, salvage routes and surface societies have no established common ancestry.

cycles.title: Our Brief Meridian
cycles.description: Courtly lives lead into the familiar scale of dates, cafes and political power. This proposed turn also accommodates ten thousand years of later reconstruction and societies with sharply different neighboring technologies.
cycles.sequenceNote: Our ordinary magicless modernity belongs in the Long Dark. The pharaohs retain their roughly ten-thousand-year local gap; the Great Wall's five centuries remain regional.

cycles.title: The Fourth Unlit Turn
cycles.description: Another dungeon culture, a new family modernity, networked control and technological war occupy a further turn. Its later points reach different ruined cities and a queen's recovered capital.
cycles.sequenceNote: Modern appearances recur after the familiar island. Synthetic combat remains material; the courts and the machines retain independent histories.

cycles.title: The Distant Habitable
cycles.description: Another court precedes another intimate modern life. Cities grow rooms, orbital inhabitants misremember the surface, and later civic worlds preserve disputed histories in memories and navigation songs.
cycles.sequenceNote: The apartment, station, memory city and fleet are individually placed societies. Their proposed succession establishes no direct descent or common catastrophe.

cycles.title: Before the Answering Sky
cycles.description: Royal households return far into material history. Inventions, a successor Earth and ancient stellar routes approach the boundary where a different kind of relation becomes possible.
cycles.sequenceNote: Material events remain magicless. Ruth's station story is positioned only by her proposed living-world endpoint; its afterlife remains undated. Reawakening follows this represented turn.

cycles.title: The Answering Dawn
cycles.description: The first reciprocal link opens this history. Much later within the proposed turn, another kingdom, private foresight, domestic obligations and urban inheritance show possible new magical societies.
cycles.sequenceNote: Only the first link's place after perfect zero is fixed. Later slots contain proposed independent systems, not demonstrated descendants of that link.

cycles.title: The Second Open Horizon
cycles.description: Another pastoral society, retired adventurers and an anxious modern family occupy separate reaches. Later, an infernal household sends a child toward college, towns remember obligations and travelers return from unsynchronized clocks.
cycles.sequenceNote: Recurring modern and courtly forms receive another chronological turn. The assignment story provisionally locates its home frame here; none of its ten destinations inherits that coordinate.

cycles.title: The World Grows Old Again
cycles.description: An old monarchy appears deep into new history. Later lives contend with borrowed years, public transformations and divine office. An expedition meets an unexplained sea, and a mill town meets a higher-order machine.
cycles.sequenceNote: Local antiquity can develop after reawakening. The monarchy's rite, possession, transit and machine remain independent systems without an asserted common origin.

cycles.title: The Farther Turning
cycles.description: A siege is followed across proposed distances by another urban age of changed identities, families and hero institutions. Crossing markets and an impossible road trip occupy separate points.
cycles.sequenceNote: The siege's three nights stay local. The later familiar societies are proposed; the road trip's altered desert retains its unsettled clocks.

cycles.title: A Familiar Future
cycles.description: Yet another modernity holds colleges, households, public body classifications and private impossible time. Familiar rooms recur far from the first modern stories.
cycles.sequenceNote: Independent magical modernities receive distant future places. Fenwick's family intervals remain intact; Cusco identifies a setting, not a Galactic date.

cycles.title: The Last Visible Horizon
cycles.description: The furthest plotted turn returns to ordinary intimacy before opening toward civic magic and a long personal past. Late therapy looks back roughly twenty-five thousand years without closing the universe's future.
cycles.sequenceNote: This is the current atlas horizon, not the world's end. The First Wound is located by its therapy frame; its remembered battle retains an unresolved earlier coordinate.

where-the-white-elk-went.note: The guardian's remembered span exceeds local kingdoms. A far-past position gives that longevity room while leaving the world outside the boundary older and unknown.

the-villages-only-mage.note: A remote village already belongs to a wider world of traveling mages. Its early position centers on the community's encounter with that wider magical culture.

blood-types-of-immortality.note: The sorcerer's blood discoveries belong to one research history. They provisionally precede later institutional healing without claiming those healers learned from this work.

never-a-mascot.note: The warrior's change from ridiculed soldier to legend takes years. It supplies an early local war history separate from later crowns and campaigns.

a-little-winter-for-sale.note: A desert trading city already purchases a dragon's work. Commerce, specialized labor and urban life are well established in this far-past society.

the-lions-last-constellation.note: A magical champion faces a mythic local task. This earlier proposed occurrence of the magical-girl form is distant from the crowded modern sky, without an asserted lineage.

fourth-house.note: An established three-house classification is challenged. The institution already has a history when this new category appears late in the turn.

the-friends-i-built.note: Cinder Annex combines engineered craft, living collaborators and formal education. This old-history slot is tentative: the Annex's physical-world relation and side of zero remain unknown.

a-crown-of-quiet-hours.note: The dragons have 218 years of rule before the Charter and seven-month works. Their local reform stays together, far from the unrelated Sleepless Majesty government.

the-door-knows-home.note: The family's traveling door requires an existing craft and repair culture. This old civic crossing history sits late in the first represented turn.

the-kingdom-of-later.note: The fairy-tale kingdom has developed habits that delay daily life. It begins another proposed turn after earlier urban histories; kingdoms can recur.

the-weight-of-falling-up-rune-shoes.note: The flying assessment belongs to an established school. It occupies a separate age after the earlier classification tale, with no institutional succession implied.

not-about-that.note: Magical girls are numerous in the everyday sky. This modernity is placed well before Northbridge and the Bay, giving the intended arc a genuinely distant beginning.

fifty-seven-minutes.note: The shipwright's fifty-seven-minute divine office belongs to one mature coastal community. Its later position keeps local god-making distinct from the preceding public-power modernity.

the-gentlest-terror.note: Dragon alliances already organize noble households. This kingdom is a courtly recurrence after a modern-shaped age, separate from the first turn's dragon government.

mother-of-monsters.note: The sanctuary has accumulated refugees before the army arrives. This later kingdom's conflict grows from an established history of displacement and protection.

the-name-the-water-took.note: Retrieved objects retain one-use sensory fragments. A tentative active-history slot preserves that unresolved effect without calling it magicless technology or connecting it to neural memory markets.

tea-for-the-first-guest.note: The wizard has lived roughly two thousand years and waited centuries for company. That local duration stays inside this slot; the tower does not survive extinction by implication.

the-morning-her-hand-moved.note: A thousand years of local ledgers precede the inhabited hand's movement. The settlement has a deep history; the colossus's underlying mechanism remains unknown.

the-ninety-year-barrier.note: Ninety years of the witch's work precede the child's breach. That whole undertaking lies within one locality near this turn's end.

when-the-eagle-bowed.note: The Eagle Queen's execution is already a century past. Her return begins a later proposed turn, separate from the preceding dragon-allied dynasty.

the-shape-of-mercy.note: A mage lineage has mature expectations about its children's powers. It provisionally precedes this turn's low-magic modern endpoint without supplying other systems' origins.

the-unfinished-sunset.note: The ronin returns after twenty years. The village's held sunset and the years outside it give this event two different experiences of the same local interval.

the-last-thing-i-could-fix.note: The smith's reputation requires developed magical craft and heroic equipment. That mature repair culture is placed before this turn's laboratory-and-school modernity.

a-note-of-spite.note: Protective spells have become a social custom. This mature magical society receives a position before Nell and Bash's ordinary world that treats magic as myth.

an-ordinary-education.note: Laboratory creation and school life coexist with active magic. This placement makes technology part of old history before the later low-magic trough.

clerics-infernal-ex.note: Sanctuary and kiln court have their own bearer-powered crossings. A separate point keeps that route outside Nell and Bash's Glass Gate chronology.

the-small-moon-rose-first.note: This point locates Nell and Bash's old low-magic material endpoint before the Glass Sea. The 617 Ravel days, eleven Earth seconds and four-month offset keep distinct clocks; Ravel remains unassigned.

every-flower-she-knew.note: Eleven flowering seasons precede one storm-bound harvest. This later rural setting is proposed; the bounded medicine proves neither an ordinary botanical cause nor a shared magical system.

a-crown-for-the-endless-fire.note: The furnace tender and six candle states expose an inherited working older than the repair. This tentative old-history point leaves the fire's underlying category unresolved.

the-sister-behind-her-smile.note: A noble household confronts one sister's change. This court is placed early in a later turn, long after the earlier dynastic histories.

voice-of-silence.note: Kethra's examination establishes her archmage qualification. Her proposed point immediately precedes her later teaching story, with the actual interval undated.

a-lock-on-the-inside.note: The same qualified archmage takes a mistreated apprentice. It follows Voice of Silence in one local lifetime-scale sequence; no measured delay is added.

the-second-wearing.note: The boxed interval cannot be measured, but the niece's inheritance supplies a living endpoint. That endpoint is provisionally here; maker and earlier storage remain undated.

the-attendance-ledger.note: Six months of Night Clerk support precede the showcase. This modernity is proposed much later than Not About That and before the Bay, without a common institution.

the-help-network.note: The opening is the third afternoon after the showcase; the network grows over months. It stays beside Attendance Ledger; its distant-before-Bay placement is editorial.

the-thousandth-fall.note: Repeated training develops a local use of self-healing. This later discipline retains its own duration without becoming the source of other healer stories.

saint-and-demon.note: The opposed callings belong to an established religious world. Their relationship is placed late in this turn; the wider theology and its historical origins remain local.

the-night-harvest.note: Three months after the creatures appear, six nights of evidence lead to the node convergence. A proposed active-history slot preserves the effect's unknown category without asserting material-zero technology.

the-peace-they-could-sleep-through.note: Two centuries of the Sleepless Majesty's files precede the grain dispute. This dragon polity is far from the first turn's Charter government, with no shared cast or sequel.

the-healers-measure.note: Training and witchknight qualification require sustained local work. A separate proposed pre-Bay position does not make this the battle's medical institution.

head-priests-in-love.note: The relationship presupposes two established local faiths. Their conflict occupies an earlier reach of the turn that eventually contains the Bay.

solstice-evening-bell.note: The Bay precedes the Glass-Sea era. It follows the earlier proposed magical-girl modernities, while its actual civil date and Galactic coordinate remain open.

the-dress-they-brought-her.note: The intended sequence places the damaged identification system after the Bay and before the museum. The prisoner is a different woman from Solstice; this is a nearby aftermath point.

the-count-was-131072.note: Solstice visits the museum centuries after the battle. One cycle preserves that local interval; the museum's pre-extinction side is proposed, not an established date.

stay-out-of-my-city.note: Brackenport's ultimatum and the daughter's departure are nine local years apart. This independent modernity is proposed after the Bay arc without inventing an invasion response.

the-bride-who-came-back.note: Winter tribute has become an established bargain between these kingdoms. Their courtly world appears after the modern-shaped Bay and Brackenport histories in this proposal.

the-future-that-refused-us.note: The broken prophecy leaves its own immediate aftermath and cost. A late-turn point separates this local predictive system from the next turn's succession histories.

the-vacant-throne.note: Fifteen years of vacancy end in the child's arrival. This kingdom is proposed in the final old turn; its compact and remembered gestures remain local.

strength-of-ten.note: Ninepin is explicitly pre-extinction. Its five-day deployment and return before day twenty remain one campaign; the distance from other old histories is proposed.

where-it-hurts.note: The emotional-wounding sword already has an adventurer-world reputation. This later old-history point remains independent of Ninepin's scar-lattice and military institutions.

daughter-of-the-sun.note: The Glass Sea follows Nell and Bash's modernity and Solstice's Bay. Day of Glass and second dawn remain four local centuries apart here, before extinction.

the-seventh-night.note: The adventurer's recurring curse belongs to active old history in this proposal. Its personal cycle remains within a late old-world society.

what-i-hate-most.note: The engineered confrontation belongs to a separate advanced magical society. A late old-history position does not derive its technology from the Glass Sea.

the-way-around.note: The desert labyrinth is already ancient on the hunter's arrival. A late old-history point allows that local past without assigning the labyrinth to a terminal system.

the-last-flames.note: The keeper's long memory precedes the young dragons' sudden arrival. The unnamed threat remains unresolved even though this story is placed late in old history.

a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.note: The dream relay follows sixty years of separation during explicitly pre-extinction imprisonment. Both episodes remain on the old side; the entity is not placed inside zero.

all-accounts-due.note: Faris's thirty-one-year accumulation ends at the fixed extinction boundary. Every proposed old-history point precedes it; no old magical capacity enters the following cycles.

four-million-falling.note: The reactor city belongs to a culture saying magic has long died. This early represented zero point allows inherited machinery to fail without making reactors surviving magic.

the-weight-they-never-counted.note: A caravan recognizes bodily strength the village undervalued. This later material society has nonhuman biological capacities without requiring operative magic.

golden-lion.note: The cane exposes surviving people behind a supposedly extinct House. This civic world has already lived through a violent break in its own political history.

the-mercy-circuit.note: Bionic and implant repair requires a mature technological economy. It forms one material modernity early in the zero, far from the later synthetic-body histories.

the-unfixed-face.note: Widely available genetic modification produces another embodied modernity. Its later position is editorial; no common lineage with the repair kiosk is established.

the-walls-are-thick-enough.note: The imperial marriage and garden scene need no enchantment. This later courtly recurrence can occupy material history after an advanced city.

last-watcher-of-jupiter.note: Thirty years of Jovian watch precede the machines' turn toward deep space. This separate orbital civilization is not another story's station or a surviving magical defense.

the-room-that-waited.note: A modernity falls without firing its arsenal; agrarian descendants enter the sealed room. Both local stages stay here, separate from the floating city's collapse.

the-ordinary-slime.note: Observation changes how a locally ordinary organism is handled. This material community is placed late in the turn; its relation to the earlier collapse is unknown.

four-crowns-in-hiding.note: Four royal sisters take refuge in smaller kingdoms. Another network of material courts opens this later turn, with its own dynasties and threats.

the-five-minute-warranty.note: Goblin engineering sustains practical inventions with short working lives. This community occupies another industrial age early in the second represented material turn.

everyone-knows-her.note: An annual urban festival frames an ordinary recognition puzzle. This familiar modernity occupies a different cycle from the cafe story and our proposed present island.

the-city-of-eleven-foundations.note: Many architectural and technological styles coexist in one city. Its districts share a present despite their very different appearances.

the-kill-she-wouldnt-take.note: Televised combat and bodily rebuilding imply mature engineered public life. This later-turn culture is independent of the preceding cycle's genetic society.

coiled-together.note: The serpentfolk queen's care is a local bodily and cultural fact. This later court can exist within material history without invoking enchantment.

the-shadow-that-nested.note: An ancient sunshade supports a living migration. The crew's present is placed here; earlier builders remain undated and unrelated to Jovian Station.

leave-the-names.note: The salvage code is older than the caravan's dead cities. Its late-turn position accommodates that deep local past without assigning the ruins to a known collapse.

only-eighteen.note: Almost two centuries of caregiving precede eighteen human years with the twins. The household's entire story remains local, while its members experience that duration differently.

a-crown-in-the-bargain.note: A political marriage confronts two people's plans. This court opens another material turn, far from the pre-extinction Ninepin negotiation it echoes.

the-courtesy-of-blades.note: The duel and courtship belong to an established culture of blades and conventions. This local society precedes the turn's familiar modern island.

before-she-gets-tired.note: Friends discuss an ordinary romantic decision. Their brief conversation belongs near the proposed familiar modern island, where deep history gives way to one person's immediate uncertainty.

the-names-on-the-cups.note: Hinge's story runs from early autumn to the first Sunday in May. One ordinary interval stays near the proposed present without imposing a shared city on other romances.

empire-within.note: The crime boss's three sleepless days belong to a material political modernity. This neighboring proposed date remains independent of the cafe and its cast.

the-ten-thousand-year-queen.note: Reconstructed adults arrive roughly ten thousand years after their genetic sources, with four further years to later contracts. This present-centered cycle keeps that local gap; reconstruction is not continuous memory or resurrection.

deja-vu-too-late.note: A one-charge neural baseline is restored after the loss. This later engineered society stays material: the outside world and its consequences have not rewound.

terms-at-four.note: An orbital platform supplies leverage during a domestic tea party. This later political modernity is not a continuation of Jovian defense or another exodus.

the-lights-beyond.note: The scouts cross five hundred years after a local war and meet a contemporaneous illuminated city. Their technological difference remains geographic, not successive universal stages.

the-last-monster.note: The dungeon inhabitants and lost adventurer require no operative enchantment for their conflict. This local material society opens another distant turn.

blade-calls-your-name.note: The blade belongs to a local craft and social world. This point offers another material-age history, distant from the earlier duel and House societies.

the-other-twin.note: The siblings' shared body and puberty belong to an ordinary embodied modernity. This familiar life is placed in a later material turn, beyond the present-centered island.

the-thirteenth-command.note: The combat-controller update is an engineered event. Its point marks a separate technological society; class terminology is not evidence of surviving magic.

drone-down.note: Police drones are routine enough to produce a teenage counterculture. This separate networked modernity has no established city or sequence shared with the driver story.

what-she-remembered-of-peace.note: Android rehabilitation precedes renewed war and old programming. That local peace-to-war sequence stays together, without turning the conflict into a universal collapse.

the-body-called-one.note: Four years in Unit 02 precede extraction and a courier flight. This later stellar conflict is independent of the android's war and the other pilot's neural restoration.

the-upward-rain.note: The expedition's instruments observe an upward sea over a drowned city without explaining its cause. Its present is tentatively placed in this active era; the site's earlier sinking and the anomaly's mechanism remain undated.

the-door-in-the-ivy.note: Clarimond retakes her capital seventeen years after leaving. This later courtly society is another material recurrence, not an inferred descendant of submerged ruins.

save-that-dragon.note: A queen asks that a dragon be protected from her daughter. Ropes and winches ground the rescue in physical work; its place in this later material court is tentative, with the dragon's fire unclassified.

sakura-hearted.note: Domestic machinery and a private evening belong to a technological household. A familiar modern life appears again far beyond the present-centered island.

a-little-more-room.note: The android neighbor's arrival develops through hallway encounters. This nearby but independent material modernity gains no shared city or cast from similar domestic technology.

the-driver-the-city-could-not-see.note: An unregistered passenger exposes an autonomous city's limits. This separate networked society lies after the drone-policed city without an asserted succession.

rooms-before-sunrise.note: Engineered living apartments make the worker's overnight deadline possible. Their present occupies this material turn; living tissue does not prove surviving old magic.

kite-letters-below.note: Eight centuries of false teaching precede the kite correspondence. The mechanic's present is proposed here, independently of all other orbital civilizations.

the-foundations-remember.note: The active rail line and neural extraction belong to a city denying older civilizations. This is its present, not an archaeological frame or a sequel to the orbital correspondence.

the-unfixed-song.note: Generations of routes precede the archive's standardization offer. This late-turn migratory society keeps its inheritance without required descent from the earlier memory city.

late-for-dinner.note: The general's household and legion belong to a recurring material kingdom. This domestic conflict opens the last represented turn before reawakening.

the-kingdom-was-the-easy-part.note: The adventurers' retired life follows their public victories. Lantern lights sustained by breath and attention require an active magical history; this later kingdom's position after reawakening is proposed.

the-rule-between-courses.note: Catfolk instincts and the restaurant's inherited rule form a local biological and social history. An established dining culture occupies this late material age.

laughing-clouds.note: The annual festival implies mature engineering and a history of repurposed failures. Another inventive city has developed deep into the long magicless interval.

apes-in-orbit.note: Human departure precedes the dinosaur surface polity and orbital remnant. Both local endpoints stay together here without dating any other station by that exodus.

the-star-that-followed-the-bells.note: The shepherd encounters a living starship with damaged memory. This separate late material inheritance makes neither the ship nor its flock a spell system.

the-first-people.note: The courier reaches humanity as the makers of ancient stellar roads. This late proposed material setting preserves deep human antiquity without identifying those roads with the nearby ship.

the-station-between.note: This tentative point locates only Ruth's familiar material-life endpoint before reawakening. Her station and trains remain outside material dating, not active magic within the Long Dark.

the-sky-remembers-us-return.note: Ordinary light crosses the whole Long Dark from the All Accounts aftermath. This point is the first reciprocal link, the fixed new-magic beginning; the earlier fall is not moved here.

where-no-unicorn-stands.note: The queen's magic and storm wards exclude material zero. A later kingdom in this first proposed new turn gives courts a future without deriving their wards from the first link.

the-night-she-knew.note: Private clairvoyance exists in a familiar household. This later modernity is proposed after reawakening, without assuming the power was secret everywhere or newly invented.

by-tooth-and-threshold.note: The visitor arrives days after the trapped wolf's rescue. That local sequence stays together in this later household, without common ancestry for other transformations.

anatomy-of-a-god.note: The confrontation presupposes practical knowledge of bodies called divine. A mature society later in the first new turn has already learned something about their limits.

the-inheritance-remembers.note: The threshold working activates during demolition in a developed civic world. Its generations fit within new history; its road is unrelated to autonomous-city networks.

the-first-kingdom-was-late-on-taxes.note: The intact village arrives at an excavation millions of years after departure. This point tentatively places the arrival in new history; departure and mechanism keep separate unresolved coordinates.

there-goes-your-name.note: The theft and chosen name belong to a pastoral locality with active magic. A second post-return turn is proposed, separate from earlier kingdoms and later superhero names.

self-reflection.note: Anin's independent life lasts four dawns in a modern household. The entire incident stays at one point in this later proposed modernity, not across multiple cycles.

life-with-a-girlfriend-with-shrinking-po.note: Shrinking is woven into an intimate modern life. This separate point stays distant from Shalegate's beast effect without proposing one size-changing tradition.

his-infernal-majesty-says-no.note: The private infernal gate reaches a contemporary human engineering college. Only the human frame is proposed here; the infernal realm gains no Galactic coordinate.

captive-couples.note: Established hero and villain identities shape two marriages. This public-power culture occupies a later post-return age; its institutions have no established ancestry in Northbridge or the Bay.

what-the-town-owed-her.note: Generations of obligations precede the town's encounter with its youthful witch. This late point allows local antiquity after return without making promise-binding surviving solar fire.

tenth-world-lesson.note: Ryo leaves and returns through the same apartment doorway. Only the home frame is proposed here; ten destinations and their assignment clocks remain separately undated.

the-hollow-cask.note: A twelve-week reopening plan meets living Underbreath in old timber. Local age fits this proposed later turn; neither the building nor colony is said to cross extinction.

a-throne-neither-wanted.note: Three centuries of forecasting records precede roughly a year of suspended injury. These local spans fit a later new-history kingdom; rite and office remain unrelated to earlier crowns.

thirteen-years-borrowed.note: Thirteen years of searching end in a bounded encounter through a living host. The full search stays within this proposed point without an era-spanning possession lineage.

what-turned-eighteen.note: Public true-form recognition is established before one eighteenth birthday. This later society retains its own classification history, separate from previous private transformations.

deaths-patron.note: A god seeks one person's earthly championship. It occupies a distinct later divine setting, not the pantheon of the first new turn's anatomical confrontation.

lightning-carries-one.note: Observed costs limit one person's lightning transit. This later civic modernity is proposed without a common network of gates, buses or dreams.

the-hoarders-house.note: The museum already employs agents to handle dangerous artifacts. This later position gives collection local time to accumulate; the objects gain no assumed old-system survival.

the-players-above.note: The mill town confronts a higher-order machine through practical engineering. This tentative active-history point leaves the machine's ontology and external perspective undated.

friends-of-the-night.note: Six years of proximity precede Shalegate's three-night siege. The entire local history sits in another later kingdom; its beasts are not successors of Night Harvest creatures.

the-wrong-side-of-the-part.note: The wig changes its wearer within a modern setting. This event has a later post-return place, while the artifact's maker and earlier history remain unknown.

the-bat-at-the-door.note: The daughter's care for a bat precedes the visitors' godparent request. Those days remain together in a household placed within this later magical modernity.

transitions-in-common.note: The friendship reveals a difference between gender and shapeshifting. This ordinary-looking magical society is placed in a later turn, with its own local conventions.

the-name-i-kept.note: A hero family has already disowned an older sibling. This later public-power culture is separated from the captured couples and magical girls, with no common institution.

realms.note: Phones, a hospital and a tablet coexist with the living Queen Street seam. This later proposed modernity preserves the return window without joining Deepmarket to another gate.

gods-afraid-of-grandma.note: The grandmother's continued earthly life involves local gods. Its late point is distinct from earlier divine societies and the future Cusco household.

roads-under-impossible-stars.note: The road trip changes under an anomalous sky. Only its living departure frame is tentatively here; altered roads and experienced reversals retain unsettled clocks.

the-warmest-person-in-the-room.note: The superhero college already teaches a cursed prodigy. This distant public-power modernity is separated from Northbridge's school and the other hero families.

the-cat-who-had-enough.note: The inherited cat's advice belongs to an established household arrangement. This far-future point locates the present exchange; the cat's earlier history remains undated.

a-darkness-written-under-skin.note: Twenty years of presumed absence precede ultraviolet discovery of living birth channels. This active-history point is proposed after reawakening; the society is not placed in material zero.

she-literally-has-wings.note: Marriage and overlooked bodily identity unfold in a familiar magical household. This far-future society accommodates the extraordinary within an established ordinary life.

the-trouble-with-tuesdays.note: Forty-six activations, seven Tuesdays to the audit and Rose's later nine-day overwrite keep one family sequence. This later frame is proposed; the watch is not an extinct-system survivor.

where-sleep-takes-you.note: Sleep-triggered travel complicates an existing modern life. This far-future position preserves the individual's local limits; no common network with other crossing stories is established.

connections.label: The light that reaches another sky
connections.note: The established chronology and return story continue Faris and Seyathi’s final fall, then follow ordinary light across ages of perfect zero. Their deaths remain final and no old system returns.

connections.label: One world, a later age
connections.note: The established chronology places Nell and Bash’s old-modern endpoint long before the Glass-Sea era on the same physical world. This orders that endpoint only; Ravel remains undated.

connections.label: The world survives to the Glass Sea
connections.note: The established western-bay chronology places Solstice’s battle before the later Glass-Sea era. No common magical system or measured interval is established.

connections.label: Three afternoons later

connections.label: Mutual aid before the Bay
connections.note: The intended reading sequence places The Help Network after The Attendance Ledger and before Solstice Evening Bell. Northbridge is proposed in an earlier cycle than the Bay; that distance is editorial, with no dated interval or institutional ancestry.

connections.label: A crowded sky, then the Bay
connections.note: The intended sequence locates Not About That before Solstice, when magical girls are numerous. The timeline proposes a separate earlier cycle before Northbridge as well; only the pre-Bay reading order is supplied, not a measured gap.

connections.label: The aftermath misidentifies a survivor
connections.note: The intended reading sequence places Dress after Solstice and before Count. Its damaged post-battle institutions turn ordinary booking marks into a false survivor claim. The prisoner is not Solstice.

connections.label: From misidentification to misremembrance
connections.note: The subplot’s intended reading sequence places Dress between Solstice and Count, without an established interval. The prisoner and the later museum witness are different people.

connections.label: The witness corrects the count
connections.note: The prose identifies its living witness as Solstice Evening Bell, centuries after the same Battle of the Bay. Both points remain in one proposed cycle to preserve that local interval; the museum's pre-extinction side remains editorial.

connections.label: The archmage becomes a teacher
connections.note: Voice establishes Kethra’s qualification; Lock begins with the same named archmage taking a mistreated apprentice and uses her call-link practice. The interval is not dated.

connections.label: Two arrangements for twelve dragons
connections.note: Indirect parallel across distant proposed cycles: Kharost's rotating Crown offices and Varkesh's collective Sleepless Majesty make different bargains with governance and sleep. No common cast, state or sequel is established.

connections.label: A home is also a living body
connections.note: Agnes exposes coerced structural labor; Lirenn discovers occupied volume inside living leased rooms. The ethical echo crosses proposed eras without asserting shared biology or building lineage.

connections.label: Who can claim a memory?
connections.note: One-use sensory fragments from retrieved objects and licensed neural extraction make distinct memory problems. The resemblance is thematic, not a shared substance or technological ancestry.

connections.label: The record beneath the monument
connections.note: A museum’s heroic reconstruction and a drowned-king interpretation meet more limited evidence. This is a reader parallel about misremembered history, not a common archive.

connections.label: Humanity becomes an inheritance
connections.note: A dinosaur surface polity and a later stellar courier encounter different human legacies. No common departure, station network, or absolute order is established.

connections.label: Learning what the creatures actually do
connections.note: Route observations change how people respond to shadow beasts and throat-node-bearing creatures. The stories establish no common species, invasion, or mechanism.

connections.label: A useful organism changes the question
connections.note: Both communities must reconsider handling practices after observing effects. The slime’s material behavior does not classify the Night Harvest effect or date either settlement.

connections.label: When the ground stops being a promise
connections.note: Evacuation requires precise counts when an inhabited hand moves and when Orison loses lift. The colossus is not assigned a reactor cause; these are not the same fall.

connections.label: The past arrives in a new present
connections.note: An intact displaced village and genetically reconstructed adults confront later institutions. Actual temporal transport and reconstruction remain different processes, not one refounding event.

connections.label: A person falls outside the map
connections.note: A threshold working disrupts a public road; a networked city cannot place an unregistered passenger. The people, technologies, and causes differ, despite the shared recognition problem.

connections.label: The destination keeps its own clock
connections.note: An assignment sequence and the Ravel encounter both resist a flat timeline. Their resemblance proves neither one portal network nor that Ryo’s destinations are Ravel.

connections.label: Crossings bring obligations home
connections.note: Bearer-powered sanctuary crossings and a living market seam both impose local limits. No mechanism, underworld, or ancient route is shared by implication.

connections.label: Company at a threshold
connections.note: Borrowed living hosts and a stranded afterlife traveler create different obligations to another person. The parallel establishes no common possession or station mechanism.

connections.label: A political offer needs a person’s answer
connections.note: Royal negotiation meets the independent will of the people inside it. This is an ethical parallel between unrelated courts, not a dynasty or a continuation of Ninepin.

connections.label: What the inherited promise costs
connections.note: A solar polity and a witch’s town confront responsibilities accumulated over generations. The juxtaposition does not make promise-binding a descendant of solar fire.

connections.label: A name that can be chosen
connections.note: Different pressures around names and identity invite a joint reading. The stories do not share a name-magic rule, heroic lineage, or cast.

connections.label: One family, unequal capacities
connections.note: An elf caregiver and the mortal eldest of a divine household feel limits differently from those around them. Longevity is not treated as proof that the two families occupy the same era.
